messages.subject: Matrix update, dgTMatrix
messages.body_plain:
Hi All,
I'm posting this to hopefully save someone a little headache as I didn't find the Matrix package documentation particularly easy to read.

Previously, one could use e.g. Matrix::bdiag(my_list) to set up sparse matrices in a block diagonal format directly readable by TMB's DATA_SPARSE_MATRIX structure.  But now, one gets an error

Expected sparse matrix of class 'dgTMatrix'

when executing TMB::MakeADFun() using this approach.  Presumably there has been some changes to Matrix as to default classes when using Matrix::bdiag().  The solution ended up being wrapping Matrix::bdiag() with as(,"generalMatrix").

Cheers, Paul

messages.subject: Which organizations use TMB?
messages.body_plain:
I am at Institute for Health Metrics & Evaluation (IHME) and we are interested in knowing the "size" of the TMB user community. Looking around I can see us, fish researchers, and NOAA. Who else is using TMB?

Cheers
Geoffrey Phipps

messages.subject: oneStepPredict() with composition data
messages.body_plain:
Hi y'all,

I want to calculate OSA residuals for my TMB model and have found success using oneStepPredict() on the total catch data (a data vector), but not the catch compositions (a data matrix). I get warnings and indexing errors when I try.

Is it possible to use oneStepPredict() on composition data?
For those using WHAM, I note that in that code, a single vector with all observations "obsvec" is made to help run the oneStepPredict() function. Is that necessary in my case too, perhaps?

Any insight greatly appreciated,
Emily Liljestrand
Michigan State University

messages.subject: Re: [TMB users] Error `file too big`
messages.body_plain:
Hi Jim,

I've run into this error before with devtools::check(). When looking into the issue, I found that devtools::check() will compile in debugger mode (the -g flag in your compiler output). I have found this <https://digitalkarabela.com/mingw-w64-how-to-fix-file-too-big-too-many-sections/> resource that recommends adding a g++ compiler flag: -WA, -mbig-obj, but I haven't been able to get this to work. My work around, as you mentioned, is to compile first (which runs gcc without the debugger) and then call devtools::check or document. I am interested in hearing if anyone else has resolved this issue.

Cheers,
Andrea
